answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require proof of sustained useful service: each identity must continuously prove it stores real data or relays real traffic for peers, verified by random spot checks. Like a jetty that only earns its keep when boats actually dock, an identity that idles or fakes service loses standing. Forging thousands of such proofs costs real sable-dark server capacity, not just keystrokes, so by dawn the honest providers outnumber cheap clones and the network can weight reputation by verified service rendered.
